title: Memory-mapped registers you can poke from a host
objective: Implement a host-side 256-byte MMIO window with four registers, little- and big-endian 32-bit accessors, a read-only STATUS, a write-triggered COUNT, and a documented alignment fault.
whyThisMatters: Industrial peripherals are not 'objects with methods' — they are addresses with side effects. If you cannot show endianness and alignment as testable facts, you will mis-talk every sensor and PLC register you meet later.
evidence: C sources for the 256-byte device window and the host poke program, with incremental Git history
A captured test run showing DATA write incrementing COUNT by 1
A captured test run showing a write to STATUS leaving the stored STATUS value unchanged
A captured dump of the four bytes at DATA for the value 0x01020304 under both LE and BE 32-bit accessors
A captured unaligned 32-bit read at offset 0x09 returning the documented error, not a guessed value
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The device window is 256 bytes, byte-addressable, and exposes STATUS at 0x00 (read-only), CTRL at 0x04 (read/write), DATA at 0x08 (read/write), and COUNT at 0x0C (read-only, increments by 1 on each successful DATA write).

A write of 0x01020304 through the little-endian 32-bit accessor at DATA and a write of the same value through the big-endian 32-bit accessor produce two different 4-byte sequences in the window; both sequences are captured.
A write to offset 0x00 does not change the STATUS bytes; before and after dumps are captured.
An unaligned 32-bit read or write at offset 0x09 returns a documented error code or result and does not store or return a silently assembled 32-bit value.
